title: A Chip-scale Space-time Multiplexed Gaussian Boson Sampling Processor Beyond 10,000 Photons
authors: Yu-Xuan Fu, He-Yu Shen, Ke-Ming Hu, Jun-Jie He, Yun-Long Nie, Hang Song, Bao-Jing Liu, Le-Si Yang, Xiao-Yu Wu, Pei-Lin Du, Yu-Ze Zhu, Yi Xie, De-Hui Huang, Yu-Fei Liu, Hai Yan, Jin-Hong Chen, Yu-Lin Yu, Chuan-Yan Peng, Wen-Hao Zhou, Feng Lu, Yu-Quan Peng, Chen-Shuo Xia, Zhi-Chao Wang, Zhe-Han Li, Lin Chen, Chao-Yang Zhang, Chun-Yan Jin, Yan-Rong Zong, Xiao-Yun Xu, Jian-Peng Dou, Xiao-Tian Fang, Pei-Qi Zhou, Hao Tang, Chang-Shun Wang, Lin Yang, Xian-Min Jin
abstract: Gaussian boson sampling (GBS) has emerged as a leading photonic paradigmfor demonstrating quantum computational advantage. Nevertheless, state-ofthe-art GBS setups face practical barriers including stringent optical alignment, phase instability, and limited programmability, which impede scalable engineering deployment. The chip-scale space-time multiplexed architecturepromises to resolve these constraints, yet it strongly demands wafer-scale chipcapabilities to simultaneously satisfy stringent requirements on low loss, highprecision and high-speed modulation. Here we report the first chip-scale spacetime multiplexed GBS system, monolithically integrating high-speed electrooptic modulators, on-chip delay lines, and a time-space multiplexed interferometric network on a thin-film lithium niobate chip, operating at a 4-GHz clockrate with detection events of up to 11,059 photons within 1 millisecond. Beyond benchmarking quantum advantage, we further reconfigure the photonichardware into a GBS-powered world model for modelling physical dynamics,which achieves lower prediction error with fewer trainable readout parameters compared with a classical echo state network (ESN) baseline. Our resultsvalidate the feasibility of our endeavor towards scalable photonic quantumhardware, and pave the way for the versatile programmable applications offuture GBS quantum systems.
summary: This paper presents a breakthrough chip-scale processor for Gaussian Boson Sampling (GBS) using a space-time multiplexed architecture on lithium niobate. It not only achieves high photon counts (>10,000) but also proves the system's versatility by reconfiguring it to model complex physical dynamics with quantum advantage over classical neural network benchmarks.
main_problem: The paper addresses the practical barriers—such as alignment issues and limited programmability—that hinder the scalable deployment of Gaussian Boson Sampling (GBS) for quantum advantage demonstrations.
main_result: They report the first chip-scale space-time multiplexed GBS system capable of handling over 10,000 photons, and demonstrate its versatility by using it as a quantum-enhanced world model for physical dynamics prediction.
method: The authors utilize a monolithic, space-time multiplexed architecture on a thin-film lithium niobate chip, combining high-speed electro-optic modulators and delay lines to generate and process large-scale GBS states.
model_or_system: The physical platform is a chip-scale GBS processor built on TFLN, integrating modulators and interferometers. This system is then reconfigured to act as a quantum dynamics engine (world model) for simulating physical systems like Kármán vortex streets.
key_observables: Detection events up to 11,059 photons within 1 ms; low prediction error (MSE) compared to classical benchmarks; high photon correlation function fidelity matching GBS theory.
important_parameters: 4-GHz clock rate; 3-dB bandwidth > 67 GHz; photon count > 10,000; low loss (e.g., 0.9 dB/facet).
main_assumptions: The feasibility relies on establishing a complete wafer-scale lithium niobate photonic chip pilot line to meet stringent loss and precision requirements.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the system setup, device characterization (modulator response, loss), the generation of large-scale cluster states, and comparisons between GBS predictions and classical model predictions for fluid dynamics.
paper_structure: The paper first details the hardware realization of the space-time multiplexed GBS chip, validates its quantum statistical properties against theory, and finally demonstrates its application by reconfiguring the hardware into a quantum world model for dynamical system prediction.
why_interesting: This work directly tackles the engineering challenge of scaling photonic quantum computation by integrating complex components onto a single chip, moving GBS from a proof-of-concept experiment toward a programmable quantum hardware platform.
